content:
Let \(a^3=837+n\) and \(b^3=837-n\). Then

\[
a^3+b^3=1674 \implies (a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2)=1674=2\cdot 3^3\cdot 31.
\]

Let \(s=a+b\). Since \(a^2-ab+b^2 \ge \frac{s^2}{4}\), we get

\[
\frac{1674}{s}\ge \frac{s^2}{4} \implies s^3 \le 6696 \implies s\le 18.
\]

Positive divisors \(s\) of \(1674\) up to \(18\) are \(2,3,6,9,18\). Testing:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
s & q=1674/s \\
\hline
2 & 837 \not<4 \\
3 & 558 \not<9 \\
6 & 279 \not<36 \\
9 & 186 \not<81 \\
18 & 93
\end{array}
\]

Only \(s=18\) works. Then

\[
ab=\frac{s^2-q}{3}=\frac{324-93}{3}=77.
\]

Thus \(a,b\) are roots of

\[
t^2-18t+77=0,
\]

so \((a,b)=(11,7)\). Hence

\[
837+n=11^3=1331 \implies n=494.
\]

\[
\boxed{494}
\]
